data.command: What is T1548.003 Bypass User Account Control?

data.text:
# T1548.003 — Bypass User Account Control

**T1548.003** is a sub-technique of **T1548 (Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism)** in the MITRE ATT&CK framework, under the **Privilege Escalation** tactic (it can also support Defense Evasion).

## What it is

User Account Control (UAC) is a Windows security feature (introduced in Vista) that forces processes to run with a **medium-integrity, filtered token** even when the logged-on user is a member of the local Administrators group. Actions requiring admin rights trigger a consent/credential prompt.

**Bypass UAC** refers to techniques that let an attacker go from medium integrity to **high integrity** (full admin token) **without the user ever seeing a UAC prompt**. It typically requires:
- The current user to be a member of local Administrators
- UAC set below the maximum level ("Always Notify" blocks most bypasses)

Notably, Microsoft historically did **not** treat UAC as a hard security boundary, so many bypass methods were never patched as vulnerabilities.

## Common methods

- **Registry hijack of auto-elevate binaries** — writing to `HKCU\Software\Classes\ms-settings\Shell\Open\command` (abusing `fodhelper.exe`) or `HKCU\Software\Classes\mscfile\shell\open\command` (abusing `eventvwr.exe`); since these are per-user keys, no admin rights are needed to write them
- **DLL search-order hijacking / side-loading** against auto-elevating executables (e.g., `sdclt.exe`, `computerdefaults.exe`)
- **Auto-elevating COM interfaces** — abusing elevated COM objects such as `ICmluaUtil` (CMSTPLUA) to execute commands with a high-integrity token
- **Environment variable expansion abuse** (e.g., hijacking `%windir%` resolution for scheduled tasks or system binaries)
- **Mock trusted directories** — creating paths like `C:\Windows \System32` (trailing space) to fool auto-elevation trust checks

## Tooling & usage

- **UACMe** (hfiref0x) — reference collection of 60+ documented bypass methods
- **Metasploit** `bypassuac_*` modules, **Cobalt Strike** `elevate uac-*` commands
- Observed in ransomware, loaders, and RATs (e.g., TrickBot, various APT tooling) to silently gain high integrity before deploying payloads

## Detection

- Registry writes to `HKCU\Software\Classes\...\shell\open\command` (Sysmon EID 12/13)
- Anomalous child processes of auto-elevate binaries (`fodhelper.exe` → `cmd.exe`/`powershell.exe`)
- Security EID **4688** with Token Elevation Type `%%1938` (full token) from unexpected parents
- Existing Sigma rules map directly to this sub-technique

## Mitigation

- Set UAC to **"Always Notify"** (highest level)
- Remove users from local Administrators (least privilege)
- Application control via **WDAC/AppLocker**
- Microsoft occasionally patches specific bypasses as CVEs — keep systems current

Reference: [attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1548/003](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1548/003/)
